correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the line set independently by enumerating the 7462 reduced row echelon two-spaces over F_9 and testing the Hermitian pairing on the two basis rows. Completeness over the algebraic closure follows both from the published 112-line theorem and directly: vanishing of the four Hermitian coefficients on a line with vector space W gives W=(W^[3])^perp for the ordinary dot product; cubing gives W^[3]=(W^[9])^perp, so W=W^[9] and its unique row echelon matrix is over F_9. A two-by-two residual determinant tests geometric meeting of distinct lines. The independent calculation recovered 48 and 64, quotient ((14,16),(12,18)), characteristic polynomial (T−18)(T−2)^43(T+2)^6(T+6)^12(T+10)^2, and every one of the 48 augmented Gram ranks 22 modulo 101. Replay: python /workspace/branches/independent_fermat.py (SymPy); output /workspace/branches/independent_fermat.log. The modular ranks give rational lower bounds, which attain the Picard rank 22. By adjunction a line has square −2; in a smooth surface the distinct tangent directions of intersecting lines give local intersection one. For D the excess sum, D·H=64 and D²=64(18−2)=1024, so the H-orthogonal class D−16H has square zero. Hodge index forces it to be numerically trivial; a numerically trivial line bundle on a K3 is trivial by Riemann–Roch and duality, since neither sign of a nontrivial numerically trivial bundle has a nonzero effective divisor. Thus D=16H in NS, and the 21-dimensional Gram rank is the span dimension since the span contains H and the form restricts nondegenerately. No integral index or nondeformability assertion follows.

evidence: The full line graph is the point graph of the dual generalized quadrangle of order (3,9): degree 30, two common neighbors for adjacent vertices, and ten for nonadjacent vertices. Its adjacency eigenvalues on the complement of the all-ones vector are 2 and −10, of multiplicities 90 and 21. The full line Gram rank and Picard rank are 22.

The full-graph critical-group record 1932fa3c1293 does not itself select the classical lines. The arithmetic Picard record 4c8353f211cf supplies the classical span dimension 20 and total dimension 22, not the excess-block spectrum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The full rank alone does not determine a subspace rank. The two-eigenvalue identity of the full graph is stronger: after removing block constants of the equitable partition, the shifted negative Gram is a scalar times an orthogonal projection, so the two complementary compressions determine each other's nontrivial spectrum.

evidence: Full degree 30 and classical degree 14 give 16 cross neighbors per classical line. The orbit makes the other cross degree constant, so double counting gives 48·16/64=12 and hence excess degree 18.

On the subspace W perpendicular to both block constants, P=(2I−A)/12 is a rank-21 orthogonal projection, since A has only eigenvalues 2 and −10 there (the quotient has eigenvalues 30 and 2). Write P=QQ^t with orthonormal columns and split Q by the two blocks. Then Q_C^tQ_C+Q_E^tQ_E=I_21. The classical table gives Q_C^tQ_C eigenvalues 1/3 with multiplicity 12, 2/3 with 6, 1 with 1, and 0 with 2, using equality of the nonzero spectra of Q_CQ_C^t and Q_C^tQ_C. Thus the excess compression has 2/3 with 12, 1/3 with 6, 1 with 2, and 0 with 43 in the 63-dimensional excess zero-sum space. Undoing the affine shift and adjoining the constant eigenvalue 18 gives exactly the submitted polynomial, hence its Gram rank and inertia.

Once degree 18 is known, Hodge index gives the stated divisor identity from D·H and D². Since the excess span has rank 21 and all lines together span rank 22, some classical line completes it; coordinate permutations and fourth-root scalings act transitively on classical lines while preserving the excess span, so any classical line completes it.
